title: Cross-Region Replication and Backup Verification

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch:metric` events with `metric_name=ReplicationLatency namespace=AWS/S3` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.16 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch:metric` traffic without `metric_name=ReplicationLatency namespace=AWS/S3`. Confirm UC-4.4.16 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:metric` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Monitor, GCP operations; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:metric" metric_name=ReplicationLatency namespace=AWS/S3
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.16_cross_region_replication_16"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.16 — Cross-Region Replication and Backup Verification: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudwatch:metric` for search criteria `metric_name=ReplicationLatency namespace=AWS/S3` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Cross-Region Replication and Backup Verification' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.16 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Collect S3 ReplicationTime and ReplicationLatency from CloudWatch. For RDS, use ReplicaLag. For Azure, ingest Backup job state from Monitor or automation runbooks. Alert when replication lag exceeds RPO (e.g. 15 min) or backup job fails.
visualization: Line chart (replication lag by bucket/replica), Table (failed backup jobs), Single value (max lag).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Monitor, GCP operations with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:metric`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect S3 ReplicationTime and ReplicationLatency from CloudWatch. For RDS, use ReplicaLag. For Azure, ingest Backup job state from Monitor or automation runbooks. Alert when replication lag exceeds RPO (e.g. 15 min) or backup job fails.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:metric" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:metric" metric_name=ReplicationLatency namespace=AWS/S3
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.16_cross_region_replication_16"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:metric` in `index=aws` to detect cross-region replication and backup verification. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_16_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (replication lag by bucket/replica), Table (failed backup jobs), Single value (max lag)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Monitor, GCP operations and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cross-region replication and backup verification so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
